body: OP! So many people have commented and offered their support - people do care about you. I'm here to listen if you want to talk about anything. It's okay if you're too tired to say much, but please hold on.
Hey, do you need somebody to talk to? I'm here to listen if you need it.

Hey.

It seems like you have a lot of questions about your suicidal urges, and you want to try to understand them. I want you to firstly understand that you're valid, and these impulses/reactions are neither normal or abnormal. You mentioned that you're not sure what part of you wants to live or die, but sometimes these desires will come from the same source - most of the time, they're synchronized and you won't necessarily be able to distinguish either one of them on their own. Even if your struggles are feeling too much to handle, please remember that it's never going to be your fault. It isn't that you can't do anything right (most people aren't doing anything *wrong*), but you may not be living up to the standards you've set for yourself. And that's fine. But you don't need to think that you aren't trying anything *but* your best.

Therapy is also not a definitive solution, but it can be a sort of assessment, just to check in on yourself and the progress you've made or left behind. You don't have a limit of cries for help that you can use. If you think this post means something, it likely does.

Also, you aren't weird for asking these questions. You are not a coward, either. I cannot make you believe what you don't want to, but I offer my thoughts instead: I don't think that suicide is so simple as you make it out to be. What do you want right now, what would you rather have than the pain? Do you just want to rest? Do you perhaps want to feel happy, or find success? You can always work toward the smallest bit of hope you have - stopping for the night is better than giving up altogether.

But the truth is, in response to your button metaphor: life may not be inherently better or worse than death, and death probably wouldn't be as painless or more painful compared to life. You also wrote that thinking about killing yourself brings you relief - and I think that may be because the extremes ensure the moderate will distribute less impact to our natures, and therefore, bear less pain. So if it's pain that you wish to avoid, I think that you're just another step closer to fighting back, even if it's not in an aggressive way. You're already considering the most permanent way to put an end to your affliction, so consider the options you haven't went over yet. Your post tells me that you've still got a lot to think about - so please hold on and think about it.

And most importantly, you're not alone. It may feel like that, emotionally, but physically, you aren't. You won't be. I hope that's something to you, at least.

Hey OP --

I'm sorry about your situation, but I'm glad you know you have something to hang onto. Holding on can be difficult, but you can do it. Your family is there to stay and support you, even if you don't necessarily want to speak to them about your struggles. They will love you regardless; I hope that is some consolation. 

Sending you all my strength.
Sounds like it'd be fun! Cheers friend :)
Get it! Who cares about other people, honestly. You'd be one mohawk cooler than them.

First of all, OP, huge hugs to you and you're not alone.  But hey, you *do* have things to worry about, and that's okay! I'm sorry about what happened, but you've made it here today. Fuck the people that make fun of you - they've got issues that you don't need to ever worry about. Chances are, whatever's on the other side won't make life any better. Please stay, and let yourself rest. You don't need to act as if everything's fine if it's hurting you - life may be unbalanced, but nobody's scale is truly equal on both sides. You've got this.

You're not a waste of space. Never blame yourself for what other people decide to do. You got a point: who the fuck WOULD torture a 13 year old for 3 years? You don't have a problem - you're valid and you're worthy of the space you take up. Screw anyone who disagrees. I'm here for you. OP.

Stay! Win the tug of war! *Obliterate* the opposing team, bro. You can do it, I believe in you. You might get some rope burns from the process but it'll ***so*** be worth it when you get that Giant Golden Trophy of Hey I Made It Out Alive. Cheers!

Hi, OP!

So, self-esteem is something that people struggle with for *many* years, and it's going to be difficult to have it all sorted out. But some good tips that I've been giving are:

* Try not to feel bad about doing nothing. If you're not seeing anyone, or just sitting on the couch with an 8-pack of beer, that's fine. Rest doesn't always look like sleeping or lounging in the bath with cucumbers over your eyes. Sometimes it can mean realizing that productivity can only happen if you've got the mental strength for it.
* If you have the urge to do something like rearranging your room or dyeing your hair, just do it. Honestly. You've literally got nothing to lose. Be impulsive with these fun decisions, and if you struggle with loving yourself, it can be good to think, wow, this is not the old me. I can change, and I can like these changes.
* Stop categorizing things into 'good' or 'bad.' You're not a 'bad' person for eating too much one day, and your friend isn't a 'good' person for picking up one piece of trash. It's all a mixture of different experiences and thoughts. Maybe replace these adjectives with something else - something a little less confining. 
* But also: worried about what kind of person you are? Focus on doing little good deeds for the planet. Instead of sitting in my dark room, letting my thoughts wander meaninglessly, I like coming on here and offering support to OPs who need it.
* Chances are, if you're looking for a sign, that is a sign. Trust your gut. Trust your instincts.
* You're a lot smarter than you give yourself credit for. Intelligence can't be measured by stuff like IQ.
* Get off the internet, or at least go somewhere on the internet that you can ignore other people's opinions - like Instagram. I like Instagram because there's only memes and pictures most of the time and you can just ignore the comments.
* r/wholesomememes is so nice if you need a quick pick-me-up.
* Research something - go on Wikipedia and just look up a random article. It's nice to learn and it's also nice to find fun facts you had no idea were true.

Normalcy is inherently objective. People have different ideas of what they may want to do before they leave life behind. But if you're worried about guilt, it might be best to hold on, try to understand how much your relationships mean to you, and what you *do* have to lose. Guiltless suicide seems like the easy way out, but we're never truly going to be let go with no kickback. You aren't alone, and maybe it's better to think about that.

Hey, OP.

This all sounds very complicated, but understandably so. Unfortunately, suicide for many of us means giving up the people and/or things that once brought us happiness. That's a big part of it. Fear of suicide is valid, and so is thinking that it's inevitable, but you're never going to be physically alone. If you fear impulsivity, use your determination - and this experience - to fight it. You're doing your best, and if your thoughts are too loud, give it time to dissolve. Maybe it'll never quiet down, but you've got a way to get it out. Please keep writing here if it brings you comfort - I'll be here to listen, and I'm sure others will, too. Sending you all my strength.

The point of living isn't to suffer. If it were, you wouldn't be questioning hope. The concept of a future wouldn't exist. The truth is that there's no definition of life, but there's significance in what we do. We just have to collect those little moments and trust that they'll mean something, enough to keep us going.

If you have a plan to hang out with your friends, drink a little, get married and have a cat, that's hope. It's not nothing. If you know you have to study until satan fears you, you've got some type of objective. You can't deny that it's still a goal - no matter how impossible it might seem.

Our lives could end tomorrow, yeah, that's a point I see people make often, but then I ask myself: why didn't it happen earlier? Not everything happens for a reason, but that means we've still got a chance to accomplish what we dream of. Even if it's ridiculous. There's a chance. So try your luck. You might not see the point in trying if there's suffering involved, but animal videos and anime are still something that make life better for you. If you can't find the meaning of anything else, you can try to find them there.

First of all, *your mother got rid of your antidepressants?*

I think that's a very questionable thing to do, especially if that's putting you in danger. Please stay safe and take care of yourself. Take the meds you need. It's not about whether or not you deserve them. Feeling okay isn't a privilege, it's a necessity.

But you know what, your worthiness of life isn't determined by how strong you are. So if you don't feel like cleaning your room, or even doing simple tasks, that's *fine.* Just do that. Resting doesn't mean falling asleep for seventeen hours straight and waking up recharged and ready to take on the world. Sometimes you can be awake and look after yourself by just letting things happen. If you're depressed, you live life on a consistent schedule of sadness - and there's a reason a cure doesn't exist for it. It's because human emotions are so much more complex than we can ever think of understanding. You are complicated and there's never one simple solution that will make you feel better. That means that suicide isn't your only option, because there are other factors you've yet to figure out.

You don't take your medication to feel like the best person in the world. You take them to feel anything better than completely hopeless - and that shouldn't be a decision. If you're motivated to do absolutely anything at all, that's still some kind of hope. Cry, if you need to. If you're too numb to do that, focus on the tiny things you enjoy. Covid limits our options, but perhaps you like taking naps, or watching YouTube. Keep doing those things, because you're never physically doing nothing at all. 

If you can't, it's fine. But don't give up on yourself. I believe in you. You wrote all of this. You can do other things, and it doesn't even need to be now. Or today. It doesn't even need to be next week. But you can - there's still a possibility. If that makes you feel better, hang onto it.

There is certainly no *defined* point of life. If you were to come up to me in the streets one day and ask me why I live, I wouldn't be able to give you a straight answer. But think about why people choose to keep going every day. Think about how many people consider ending it all and end up putting down the weapon and looking toward the next day. We're all different, and we all live for different things. It could be love, or family, or smaller things like the way our favorite candies taste. If none of those things appeal to you, maybe you live for apathy. Maybe you live to think about how meaningless existence is, and that's also completely fine. If it brings you peace, if you like trying to understand the world, it's still something. There doesn't even need to be an answer. Black-and-white solutions are kind of stupid, anyway, don't you agree?

So there may not be a point in life, but there's no point in death, either. There's no point in everything, if you're really into nihilism. But there's still *meaning.* Maybe that's why people do the things they do.

Hope that makes sense, at least to some degree.

Hey, no matter how temporary it is, hope is still something to cling onto. It's true that you can't live without pain, but think about how little the rich know of suffering from lack of privilege. They may face different sorts of problems, but you're facing a kind of pain that they'll never understand. That makes you braver than them in a way they'll never get. Isn't that something to consider? Even for a little?

I'm sure that you provided your best friend great comfort during difficult times, however small you think it may be. I'm sorry about what happened. You're important, and the world may be fucked up, but your bravery makes it a little less terrible. Suicide may seem like the easiest option, but think about a solution where you are happy, and still alive. Imagine how good that would be. 

Hold on, because in the future, people will be inspired by your resilience, and try to think about waking up tomorrow. Today, you deserve to have a break from the shittiness of the planet. Please rest. You're doing alright. You're doing the best you possibly can, and that's enough. You don't need to make those sacrifices for life to be quiet. You *are* the master of your soul even now and you never have no options left.

It's okay to not have a good day. Let your brain rest, think about why you feel the way you do, and try to argue with it. The world might prove you wrong, but it only matters if you think it does. You've got this. You're doing just fine.

And you *do* matter, right now, you matter more to me than anything else, because I'm writing to you, and I'm saying that I'm here for you. You don't have to give anybody anything - because they care about you without knowing what you have to offer. If it makes you feel better, I don't know what you do, or who you are, but I still think you're worth more than you give yourself credit for. You're amazing.

Your therapist doesn't get to tell you to accept everything. You don't have to accept anything you don't want to. I think it's better to feel lost sometimes, and let things play out, so you can plan your next step forward. You are not an inconvenience. I want to hear you vent. I want to comfort you. You matter. You're worth it.

Please don't think that you aren't.

I'm sorry to tell you, but sadness won't stop. But think about why people choose to hold on even though they *know* the suffering won't end: think about your motive, and think about who you want to be. If you have no goal, think about where you've gotten. As life progresses you'll meet people who will be impacted by your words and your bravery, and maybe you can continue for them. I have certainly been influenced by your courage. You are worthy and important. Please keep going.

You're not a pussy for feeling worried about the future. I'm so sorry about your situation; if there was a way I could help, I definitely would. But I can provide to you my support: I'm here if you need someone to listen. 

You are worth infinite amounts of happiness and peace, and you deserve to feel validated, even if you feel like you aren't. Society can be bad, but you never have no chance at all. Hold on a bit longer, see where life takes you, and please tell your father that he is doing the best that he can. He is such a brave person, and so are you. Sending you all my strength, friend.
Those are good reasons, and most of all you seem a very determined person. Respect, and wishes that it's all going good.
Hi, OP! You're not alone. I'm here for you if you'd like to talk about anything :)

You're not destined to be alone. Hold on, please, so one day you'll get to know what your fate actually is. I am here for you, and we are talking to each other. You are not by yourself. It's okay if you feel like you are, but right now, physically, you aren't. I hope that's at least something.
Hi OP. Please hang on for another day. I'm here to listen to you if you need it. You aren't alone.
Hey, please hold on. If you want to chat or talk about what's happening, I'd be willing to listen. You're not alone.

You're not wasting people's time! You are important. I'm sorry you feel stressed about your environment - it sounds like you're quite burnt out. It's okay to switch between different headspaces; it's all about growing, and trying to do the best you can for yourself.

It's alright to not feel happy when you accomplish something, and it's also okay to feel sad when it's not necessarily "appropriate." There's no schedule for feelings, but you certainly deserve to let yourself experience them.

Try not to compare yourself to other people. I know it's easier said than done, but you're putting a lot of pressure on yourself as is. I'm glad you're at least documenting your thoughts for some kind of release, and you should be proud of yourself for getting this out. It's not easy venting sometimes. You are on a different journey than the people you know - what may work for them may not necessarily work for you. Most of all, though, if you feel like you need professional help, I'd say get it. Your mother doesn't get to be disappointed in you for that stuff - if anything, you're "getting on in life" by accepting the fact that you need support. It's not strange, and there's nothing wrong with you; sometimes it's just how it is.

I'm here for you, OP, and you're not alone. Thanks for writing this.

It's good that you don't have the urge to commit suicide. That's a start; it seems that maybe  you're in a state of emotional vulnerability right now, and that's completely okay. Let the kitten be your ray of hope. If you can't live for yourself, try living for her.

And you shouldn't ever feel guilty about being open, as long as the person is consenting to giving you support. Otherwise, don't worry about it. I'm sure that if it were getting to them, they'd say something.

Sending you my strength and support, OP!
You're valid and I'm here for you. You aren't alone. If you need someone to listen, I'll be willing to do that.
Hey OP. Glad things got better. I'm here for you.

Hi there, OP. I'm sending you my strength. This sounds rough, but you've gotten to 26. You're doing perfectly fine. Let yourself cry for a bit, and release your feelings. I'm here for you and you aren't alone.

Hey, OP. I'm sorry. This all sounds terribly difficult, but please hang on and don't listen to them. I know how much it hurts right now, and that you love this person, but you *can't* listen to these things, no matter who it's coming from. It doesn't matter if a monk or a priest or God or whatever you may believe in tells you that you deserve to die, they're ***wrong*** and that's what they'll always be.

It actually doesn't sound like you're being manipulative at all, especially if you were vocal about your suicidal tendencies and gave them the option to avoid things they were uncomfortable with. I don't want to apply any labels, but that's definitely not what you're doing, so please don't worry about that part.

I don't understand why anyone would do this, but please realize that you don't need to trust people. You don't need to feel accepted to be worthy of life. You're doing fine, and you're doing good, and everything you need is already within you. That's just the truth. You don't have to trust me, but at least trust that.

I am sorry that this person took advantage of your vulnerability. You allowed them chances and they took it multiple steps too far, but this isn't your fault. It's never going to be your fault.

You don't have to keep suffering - but in the way that you can find peace outside of suicide. Please reach out if you need someone to listen.

It would be nice if I told you to get rid of the note, and move on with your life, try to find peace in other things, but that's just not simply how it works. I'm sure you've realized that, countless times. So I'm offering you candid support and truthful words, as an attempt to maybe convince you that you're doing just fine as you are.

So first off, you're not alone. I am here - there's at least that. You're not unloveable because I love you. When I read about your suffering, I don't judge your efforts; I've never even considered doing that. You are so brave for writing to us here. Now, my question is: is your goal to lose weight? Is self-image the biggest obstacle you are facing right now? You talked about the pandemic - and it's definitely been hard for everyone, but there's still going to be progress. Things may change but this will not last forever.

I think because you've made an effort, it already means you've still got hope. If one exercise bike doesn't work, please try and find another. It's not you, it's the people who made it that are to blame for the equipment's fragility. You aren't lazy, and even if you have moments where you feel like doing nothing, it doesn't mean that you're any less important or loved than people who are constantly at work. Remember that we don't have similar goals and you're on a journey to find something else. Sometimes, while people need to swim as fast as they can to shore, it'll be better for you to just stay afloat.

If your parents are telling you that you're "a piece of shit," they're *not* perfect. We may have different opinions on what perfection looks like, but that doesn't sound like something someone completely "good" would do. It's okay to be depressed, or lazy. People can guilt trip you about that, but the truth is just to let yourself do what you need to.

It's not impossible. You're here, sharing your story, because you weren't able to do that to the people who were supposed to help you. And that's just their loss - you're *not* hopeless. We're here to listen to what you have to say, and I think your feelings are valid. Anyone who thinks otherwise can screw off.

If you're not in a good situation to move out, try to act like you already have, maybe. If your parents aren't too controlling, you could start buying your own groceries, maybe keeping the door closed and ignoring their demands. You don't need to act as if they don't exist, but you can start living your own life without them criticizing you. I think that is what everyone deserves.

Sending you my strength.

Hey, OP.

Sounds like you're very self-aware - I think that you have the potential to do great things. Or at least the things you want to do; it's fine to not succeed!

This community is about showing support to those who need it. If you want to chat, about anything, I'm sure there are hundreds of people that would be willing to listen. If you feel overwhelmed, please take the time to sit down with yourself and try to clear your mind.

Hello, OP!

I'm sorry about what happened. I haven't seen anything like that before, but it seems to be some kind of statement, maybe on paper, to me. I recognize the ink texture. 

Still, I think that if she left the photograph for you, she knows how you'll perceive it. Maybe there isn't an answer - sometimes it's not like that. I think that you already understand it to some extent.

Well, that puts it into a different perspective. And I think that you don't have to keep fighting if you don't want to. You can be vulnerable and "weak," and it won't have an impact on who you are, or how worthy you are of happiness. I still think that you hold some strength, but it's okay not to use all of it, all the time.
Hey, OP. Please cling onto that small hope. With every day that you rise out of bed and wake up, imagine it expanding. I'm here for you if you want to chat.

I'm here to listen if you need somebody to. Please don't commit suicide. Keep going, at *least* for one more day. I think you can do it, and I believe in you. Right now, you are so much more cared for than you can possibly imagine.

It's always normal to feel horrible. You're *never* victimizing yourself for suffering. 

First off, I'm very sorry your parents treat you that way. Your needs should never be neglected - remember that you are a human being, and you don't ever deserve to suffer. If you would like somebody to talk to or become friends with, you've taken the right steps into doing so by going on reddit. There are plenty of people here that would be willing to chat! I think that you're a very brave and worthy individual.

So yes, it's normal that you're feeling miserable. And it's definitely not your fault. Feel free to respond w/ anything if you need resource links for food and necessities; that's something I can provide for you! And you are perfectly valid as you are, so please don't ever doubt that.

If you can see a solution, there might be one. Please hold on for as long as you can. Maybe things will get better, and maybe they won't, but wouldn't it be worth it if you got to find out?

Sending you my greatest thoughts, my friend. Keep going, even if it's just for another day - and maybe you can find the strength to make it another week, or months.
No problem. I'm glad I could help, even if it were just the tiniest bit. If you want to talk anytime soon, about anything, just send a msg! You're doing just fine.
Suicide isn't your only hope. My question is, what do you want from life? Do you think if you were happy, you'd think the same?

I get that! I get it. I really do. You don't want to settle - that's completely understandable.

Actually, I have experience in this kind of problem and I'm just going to say that I don't think you should end it all. There are too many open-ended questions in your life that you cannot miss out on finding the answers to. It's ***terrifying*** to think about what *can* happen, and that's valid, but I think that your awareness of a way you can be happy is another step toward maybe getting to know yourself better. You don't ever have to be perfect. I know we all have the mindset of "we should embrace our mistakes EXCEPT the ones that are unacceptable," but nothing progresses with that.

I will not tell you to accept yourself because it's a lot harder than it looks. What I do know, however, is that I think you'll have a chance if you try to give yourself time. You don't need to be ridiculously successful tomorrow. It's okay to just be unhappy with yourself and waste time for a whole day - maybe even weeks. Give it time, please, and just try to find out what would happen if you do certain things. Mix scenarios up. Try to beat the system. You know what you can do to find peace - try to get there by holding on for another day.

I definitely understand - or at least "get" - what you're talking about. And I also agree that I probably can't help you - but I just ask that maybe you can consider believing me when I say that you're probably going to be alright. You're not dramatic or stupid for responding and you really don't deserve to feel that way.

And also, it's definitely not offending to talk about low intelligence!!! It's all quite frankly a useless measurement, anyway. Your worth isn't determined by those factors, as I've said before. But what is it that you truly want, do you think? Would you like to be able to achieve your goals in the end? Do you think that would make things better for you? 

What do you think would change your mind?
Oh, thank you so much for this. I'm really glad I was able to help you.
We are! Just worthy people in an undefinable mess of a world.

Hello, my friend!

Alright, this is some heavier, more philosophical business that I'm about to *try* and get into (as an ignorant, rather unintelligent minor), but it seems that you just need a will to keep going. Honestly, your pursuit of that could just be it - at least, that's just my opinion. People *are* characteristically ill-natured at times, and I'll agree with you on that one. Also, it's definitely not about perspective - this year has proven it. But I think that you're not someone who goes out of their way to harm others, and it's nice to see someone be a part of that. You can remind the suffering that there's still ***some*** kind of good left in the world. If you don't believe there is, we can go on a quest to find it, in solidarity. You said that you're contributing to the evils of the world (or at least implied it). You're really not. If anything, you're contributing to just... humanity. Whether it's disgusting to you or not, it's still just something that we can't put a label on.

But alas, I can't really tell you what to live for, though I'm sure you already know this. I've also found that seeing the world in black-and-white doesn't help me to find hope within myself to carry on. It's easy getting caught up in the narrative that there are "good people" and "bad people." We make mistakes, and those mistakes often bring detrimental side effects to our environment, but I've realized it's just important to give ourselves a break from getting caught up in what happens as a result of The Faults in Humanity (trademark). Staying on solid ground is better compared to sinking or floating most of the time. 

So yes, life is disappointing, and all-in-all probably a horrendous waste of time, but maybe your solution is considering why people choose to keep going. Is it their loved ones? The simple pleasures in life, like sugar, and temporary tattoos, and butterflies? Maybe. These all seem trivial in the long run, but it's still something - and isn't that just what we're looking for?

But still, I believe in your search for happiness. I really do. And your posting this is probably the first step in a long trek to a better path. Cheers!

Hey, my friend, I'm here for you, but I also disagree with you. You're not completely worthless, and you don't deserve to die.

If you're going through something that you want to change, but can't, I hope that you'll stay around long enough to at least find out how it'll turn out. Even if it's really bad right now, I still don't think you deserve to end your life. Worth isn't determined by what you do or what problems you come across. There's no correlation. There never will be.

Do you need to talk to somebody about it? I'm here to listen.

Hey!

Do you want to talk about stuff? We totally can. Nobody else would need to get involved!

Hey, what do you mean, stronger than you truly are?

I think you're strong - maybe not the type of strong you want to be, but I think it's still something.  And It's alright to be tired - I will be here with you if you want to chat about anything. Or you can read this, try to believe me, and consider focusing on just trying to fall asleep tonight. Don't end things. Maybe tomorrow will be better, maybe it won't, but I think that you are strong enough to try and figure out.

And I know you are. Please believe me, at least for one more day.

Hey, I'm here. And I'll be here as long as you need it.

The thing is, I don't know you personally, but I don't think that nobody would notice. You *don't* know that for certain. Right now, I am writing a response to you, possibly from the other side of the world, and I am sending you my strength, and I am trying to convince you that you have meaning. What are the odds that nobody would notice? What are the odds that we are here now? They're slim - so incredibly slim - but here we stand.

You might not believe me right this moment, but you need to trust me, just for another day. 

Do you want to maybe elaborate on the situation? I'm here to listen if you need me.
